question:
pp-selectid (Protocol Pulse clip-video builder). The verifier found that builds 166-168 ran "by hand": a wrapper script imported tests/package/proof_ledger.py and called main() with patched settings, through the launcher's DRIVER= override. RULING 163 (5): the build record states which driver ran and its git sha, and the launcher refuses any driver that is not the committed one; RULING 160 (2b): one outcome line per build. THE CHANGE (diff below): proof_ledger.main() now (a) refuses (exit 2, no record) unless entry_of() finds sys.modules['__main__'].__file__ is this file (realpath), or pytest with PP_SELECTID_DRIVER_UNDER_TEST=1 (set only by tests/package/conftest.py); _main() (the old body, otherwise unchanged) checks entry_of() again; (b) wraps _main in try/finally and calls outcomes.record_build(out_dir) once when box["out_dir"] was set (right after os.makedirs(out_dir)); SIGTERM -> sys.exit(143) so the finally runs; (c) writes "entry" (driver, driver_sha = git hash-object, driver_committed, argv0, HEAD, dirty files) into inputs.json. The launcher tests/package/record/build_and_record.sh (moved from a scratch folder into git, paths repo-relative) runs only tests/package/proof_ledger.py with --build-no N, and refuses (exit 6) when that driver differs from HEAD, any .py/.sh under pipeline/ or tests/package/ is changed and not committed, or HEAD has commits not pushed.
CHECK, quoting the code: (1) can a wrapper still run a build (through main(), _main(), or the launcher with DRIVER= set), and does a plain `python3 -B tests/package/proof_ledger.py ...` still pass entry_of; (2) can a build that made its record folder end with no outcome line or two (an exception inside record_build, SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt, a return before box is set); (3) bash bugs in the launcher's new guards (git diff --quiet exit codes, the status/awk/grep pipeline when nothing matches, '@{u}' with no upstream, set -u). Report only what the code shows; if unsure, say so.

consensus_findings.issue: The finally-block inner handler catches only Exception. If OC.record_build itself raises a BaseException (e.g. SystemExit from a sys.exit inside a helper, or KeyboardInterrupt during the write), it propagates uncaught, no outcome line is written, and the error is not reported to stderr. The outer except BaseException / raise has already re-raised the build's own exception, so the process dies with no RULING 160 (2b) line and no diagnostic.
consensus_findings.evidence:
except Exception as e:                       # noqa: BLE001  never masks the build's own end
                print(f"  RULING 160 (2b): the outcome line was NOT written: {type(e).__name__}: {e}",
                      file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
consensus_findings.fix: Widen the inner handler to except BaseException (or at least except (Exception, SystemExit)) so a failure inside record_build is always reported and never silently swallows the outcome line.

rejected_findings.issue: box["outcomes"] is never assigned anywhere in _main(), so path=box.get("outcomes") in the finally-block call to OC.record_build is always None. If record_build requires a valid path to locate/write data/builds/outcomes.jsonl, the single outcome line RULING 160 (2b) mandates is never written for any build that creates its record folder.
rejected_findings.evidence:
box.update(out_dir=out_dir, build_no=a.build_no)     # RULING 160 (2b): from here on, the build has one outcome
...        box["refused"] = refused                         # RULING 160 (2b): BUDGET_STOPPED at the start
...                line = OC.record_build(box["out_dir"], rc=rc, error=err, refused=box.get("refused"),
                                       build_no=box.get("build_no"), path=box.get("outcomes"))
rejected_findings.fix: Set box["outcomes"] to the outcomes.jsonl path (e.g. os.path.join(REPO, "data", "builds", "outcomes.jsonl")) alongside the existing box.update(out_dir=..., build_no=...) call, or remove the path= keyword argument if record_build derives the path from out_dir.

rejected_findings.issue: _main() has no explicit return after logf.close(), so on the normal (non-refused, non-exception) completion path it returns None. main() then passes rc=None into OC.record_build. If record_build expects an int exit code to classify the outcome (e.g. 0 = success), a None rc may produce a malformed or missing outcome line. (Unsure: the full file beyond the diff context is not visible; a return 0 may exist after logf.close().)
rejected_findings.evidence:
say(f"  RULING 107 (1): fingerprint {fp_end[:12]}, {left} item(s) left undone"
            + (f" ({len(money)} of them paid call(s) the spend stop refused)" if money else ""))
    logf.close()
rejected_findings.fix: Add return 0 after logf.close() so the success path yields an explicit int rc, or confirm in outcomes.py that record_build treats rc=None as success.

missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.issue: entry_of's pytest bypass can be triggered by a non-pytest wrapper that sets the env var and imports pytest.
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.evidence: test = os.environ.get(UNDER_TEST) == "1" and "_pytest" in sys.modules; why = None if own or test else ...
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.fix: Require an actual pytest run (e.g. PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST or a pytest-specific marker) rather than only _pytest in sys.modules, or remove the env bypass for non-pytest entry.

missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.issue: The dirty-code guard ignores untracked .py/.sh files, so new untracked code under pipeline/ or tests/package/ is not treated as uncommitted.
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.evidence: DIRTY=$(git status --porcelain -- pipeline tests/package | grep -v '^??' | awk '{print $NF}' | grep -E '\.(py|sh)$' | tr '\n' ' '); entry_of also uses if not x.startswith("??")
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.fix: Include untracked code files in the dirty check, e.g. git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- pipeline tests/package | grep -E '\.(py|sh)$'.

missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.issue: entry_of's dirty list can record a rename as the whole 'old -> new' string instead of the target path.
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.evidence: dirty = sorted(x[3:] for x in st if not x.startswith("??") and x[3:].endswith((".py", ".sh")))
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.fix: Parse porcelain rename lines (split on ' -> ') and record the target path.
